Given that the line segments $\overset{―}{CD}$ and $\overset{―}{AF}$ are parallel and $m∠FAO={(3x+18)}^{∘},$ find the measures of $∠FAO$ and $∠AOE.$

$∠FAO=$
{{field-1}}
${}^{∘}$

$∠AOE=$
{{field-2}}
${}^{∘}$
question.worked_solution:
The parallel line segments $\overset{―}{CD}∥\overset{―}{AF}$ are cut by the transversal $\overset{―}{AD}.$

The angles $∠ODC$ and $∠FAO$ are interior to the parallel line segments and are on opposite sides of the transversal. So, they are alternate interior angles and consequently, they have the same measure.

In step 4, we found that $m∠ODC=5{x}^{∘}.$

Setting the measures of $∠ODC$ and $∠FAO$ equal to each other, we have an equation that we can solve for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}m∠ODC & =m∠FAO \\ 5{x}^{∘} & =(3x+18)^{∘} \\ 5x & =3x+18 \\ 2x & =18 \\ x & =9\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting $x=9$ into the expressions for the measures of $∠FAO$ and $∠AOE$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}m∠FAO & =(3x+18)^{∘} \\  & =(3\cdot 9+18)^{∘} \\  & ={45}^{∘} \\ m∠AOE & =(185-5x)^{∘} \\  & =(185-5\cdot 9)^{∘} \\  & ={140}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, $m∠FAO={45}^{∘}$ and $m∠AOE={140}^{∘}.$

                            Find an expression in terms of $x$ for the measure of the angle $∠AOE.$

                            
                                    
                                        
                                            

                                                

                                        
                                        
                                        

                                    
                                
                                    
                                        
                                        $∠AOE=$

feedback.worked_solution:
Since $∠AOD$ is a straight angle, the angles $∠AOE$ and $∠DOE$ are supplementary. Two angles are supplementary if their measures add up to ${180}^{∘}.$ 

So, the measure of the angle $∠AOE$ that's supplementary to the angle of $∠DOE=5x-{5}^{∘}$ must be

$$
\begin{aligned}∠AOE & ={180}^{∘}-(5x-5)^{∘} \\  & =({180}^{∘}+{5}^{∘})-5{x}^{∘} \\  & ={(185-5x)}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that the points $A,C,$ and $D$ lie on the circle. We know that the radius of the circle is $r=OC.$

We first notice that

$$
AD=AO+OD.
$$

Now, $\overset{―}{AO}$ and $\overset{―}{OD}$ are both segments between the center of the circle and the circle itself. So, they are both radii of the circle, and because $AD=8,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}AD & =8 \\ AO+OD & =8 \\ r+r & =8 \\ 2r & =8 \\ r & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we obtain

$$
OC=r=4.
$$

                            Find an expression in terms of $x$ for the measure of $∠COD.$

                            
                                    
                                        
                                            

                                                

                                        
                                        
                                        

                                    
                                
                                    
                                        
                                        $m∠COD=$

                                    
                                
                                    
                            
                                        {{field-1}}                
                                    
                                
                                    
                                        
                                        ${}^{∘}$

feedback.worked_solution:
We're given that $∠BOE$ is a straight angle, so

$$
m∠BOE={180}^{∘}.
$$

Now, the angle addition postulate gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}m∠BOC+m∠COD+m∠DOE & =m∠BOE \\ (5x+5)^{∘}+m∠COD+(5x-5)^{∘} & ={180}^{∘} \\ 10{x}^{∘}+m∠COD & ={180}^{∘} \\ m∠COD & =(180-10x)^{∘}\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.worked_solution:
Since $\overset{―}{OC}$ and $\overset{―}{OD}$ are radii of the circle, the triangle $△OCD$ is isosceles. Consequently, the base angles must have the same measure:

$$
∠OCD=∠ODC.
$$

Also, from step 3, we know that $m∠COD={(180-10x)}^{∘}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14196588/assets/509c6fd7ffabd5c4f7b71e89dd94cb29c374dd6d2d64407d65bcdef44553c60e.png)

Now, since the internal angles of any triangle sum to ${180}^{∘},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}m∠ODC+m∠OCD+m∠COD & ={180}^{∘} \\ m∠ODC+(m∠ODC)+(180-10x)^{∘} & ={180}^{∘} \\ 2m∠ODC-10{x}^{∘} & ={0}^{∘} \\ 2m∠ODC & =10{x}^{∘} \\ m∠ODC & =5{x}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, $m∠ODC=5{x}^{∘}.$
